record.title: Little Nightmares III
record.description:
Little Nightmares III follows Low and Alone, two children trapped in the Spiral, a cluster of disturbing locations within the Nowhere. Their goal is to survive its residents, solve environmental puzzles and find a path out.

The game can be played solo with an AI companion or with a friend through online co-op on the same platform. Low uses a bow and Alone uses a wrench, giving the pair different ways to interact with threats, mechanisms and environmental obstacles. Friend’s Pass allows one owner to invite another player on the same platform into online co-op.

record.worldSummary: The Spiral is a cluster of eerie locations within the Nowhere, connected by the journey of Low and Alone. Each area combines oversized architecture, hostile inhabitants and environmental storytelling that makes the children feel physically vulnerable. The setting continues the Little Nightmares tradition of communicating much of its history through spaces, props and creatures rather than direct exposition.

record.verdictSummary:
Score note: 6.9/10 is a direct normalization of the current 69/100 Metacritic aggregate for the Nintendo listing; it is not a separately invented store rating.

Little Nightmares III keeps the series’ disturbing environmental style while making two-character cooperation central to puzzles and traversal. Its strongest new idea is online co-op, while the lack of couch co-op and modest Switch 2 launch performance are important limitations.
verdictPros: Strong atmosphere and environmental art direction.
Complementary character tools create useful cooperative interactions.
Online co-op adds a genuinely new way to experience the series.
verdictCons: No couch co-op despite the two-character design.
Switch 2 launch performance targets 30 FPS and can show dips/stutter.
Focused campaign length may feel short to players seeking a large adventure.

record.title: Luigi’s Mansion 3
record.description:
Luigi’s invited to the towering Last Resort hotel, but when Mario and friends go missing, our green-clad hero will have to conquer his fears to save them! Slam, blow away, and vacuum up ghosts with the all-new Poltergust G-00, and join forces with Gooigi to overcome the puzzling contraptions and mischievous boss on each themed floor. And that’s just the Last Resort. Enter the ScareScraper for 8-player local wireless* or online** co-op gameplay.

See if you can defeat all the ghosts, rescue all the toads, or clear other objectives before time runs out…in the ScareScraper! And for more mini-game madness, compete on teams at the ScreamPark! Whether you play with friends or wander the hotel alone, you’ll be sucked in by the atmospheric music and ghoulish décor of every cobwebby corner you explore. Why not take in the cinematic sights and sounds with a friend? In the main adventure, you and a friend can play together as Luigi and Gooigi in two-player co-op! Gooigi can walk on spikes, slip through tight spaces, and help Luigi overcome obstacles he can’t tackle alone. Never hurts to have a friend in this hotel; it may not be very spooky, but Luigi begs to differ!

•	Catch ghosts and solve puzzles to rescue Mario and friends in the Last Resort hotel
•	Each floor of this towering hotel is themed, from the décor to the puzzles to boss!
•	Utilize the functions of the all-new Poltergust G-00: Pummel ghosts with a Slam, break through defenses with the Suction Shot, and blow back groups with a Burst
•	Luigi can call upon and control Gooigi, his all-green doppelganger, who can do what Luigi can’t
•	Gooigi can slip through tight spaces, walk on spikes, and help Luigi overcome obstacles
•	Change between Luigi and Gooigi in single player, or let a friend play as Gooigi for 2-player co-op

record.descriptionEn:
Luigi’s invited to the towering Last Resort hotel, but when Mario and friends go missing, our green-clad hero will have to conquer his fears to save them! Slam, blow away, and vacuum up ghosts with the all-new Poltergust G-00, and join forces with Gooigi to overcome the puzzling contraptions and mischievous boss on each themed floor. And that’s just the Last Resort. Enter the ScareScraper for 8-player local wireless* or online** co-op gameplay.

See if you can defeat all the ghosts, rescue all the toads, or clear other objectives before time runs out…in the ScareScraper! And for more mini-game madness, compete on teams at the ScreamPark! Whether you play with friends or wander the hotel alone, you’ll be sucked in by the atmospheric music and ghoulish décor of every cobwebby corner you explore. Why not take in the cinematic sights and sounds with a friend? In the main adventure, you and a friend can play together as Luigi and Gooigi in two-player co-op! Gooigi can walk on spikes, slip through tight spaces, and help Luigi overcome obstacles he can’t tackle alone. Never hurts to have a friend in this hotel; it may not be very spooky, but Luigi begs to differ!

•	Catch ghosts and solve puzzles to rescue Mario and friends in the Last Resort hotel
•	Each floor of this towering hotel is themed, from the décor to the puzzles to boss!
•	Utilize the functions of the all-new Poltergust G-00: Pummel ghosts with a Slam, break through defenses with the Suction Shot, and blow back groups with a Burst
•	Luigi can call upon and control Gooigi, his all-green doppelganger, who can do what Luigi can’t
•	Gooigi can slip through tight spaces, walk on spikes, and help Luigi overcome obstacles
•	Change between Luigi and Gooigi in single player, or let a friend play as Gooigi for 2-player co-op
•	Up to 8 players can work together to ascend the ScareScraper via local wireless or online
•	It’s Team Luigi vs. Team Gooigi in a mini-game battle to see which is the ultimate team of ghost hunters

faq.q: Does Mario Golf: Super Rush support online play?
faq.a: Yes. The game supports online play for 2-4 players in supported modes.

faq.q: Does it support Nintendo Switch 2?
faq.a: Yes. Nintendo lists it as Supported – game behavior is consistent with Nintendo Switch.

faq.q: What are the main special modes?
faq.a: The game highlights Speed Golf, Battle Golf, and the single-player Golf Adventure mode.

faq.q: Does Mario Golf: Super Rush support local multiplayer?
faq.a: Yes. It supports local multiplayer, making it suitable for couch sessions and party-style rounds with friends or family.

faq.q: What makes it different from standard golf games?
faq.a: Its headline difference is Speed Golf, where players race across the course in real time after taking their shots, creating a much more frantic tempo.
